body.statement: For the exact-support witness graphs \(G_\star,H_\star\), the row exchange and nonzero source rescaling give a bijection between their complete exact-support observational mechanism spaces, and therefore \(\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(G_\star)=\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(H_\star)\).  If \(\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I\), then \(\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G_\star)\ne\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)\), including when the ambient source class has no moment restriction.  On the finite-second-moment subfamily, under \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\), every \(G_\star\) kernel satisfies \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_2,X_3)=0\), whereas every \(H_\star\) kernel has nonzero covariance; for mechanisms related by the row-exchange bijection, the latter covariance is \(-(c/a)d\sigma_L^2\ne0\).
body.proof_tex:
We first prove equality of the observational model sets without using centering or moments.  By Definition \texttt{def:witness-mechanisms}, an arbitrary mechanism on \(G_\star\) has equations
\[
 L=\varepsilon_L,\qquad
 X_1=cL+aX_2+\varepsilon_1,\qquad
 X_2=bX_1+\varepsilon_2,\qquad
 X_3=dL+\varepsilon_3,
 \tag{1}
\]
where Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} and the displayed admissibility condition give
\[
 a\ne0,\qquad b\ne0,\qquad c\ne0,\qquad d\ne0,
 \qquad 1-ab\ne0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Define the \(H_\star\) coefficients
\[
 \alpha=b^{-1},\qquad \beta=a^{-1},\qquad
 \gamma=-ca^{-1},\qquad \delta=d
 \tag{3}
\]
and define its sources on the same probability space by
\[
 \eta_L=\varepsilon_L,\qquad
 \eta_1=-b^{-1}\varepsilon_2,\qquad
 \eta_2=-a^{-1}\varepsilon_1,\qquad
 \eta_3=\varepsilon_3.
 \tag{4}
\]
Every division in (3)--(4) is licensed by (2).  Equation (4) is a permutation followed by nonzero coordinatewise rescaling.  Hence Assumption \texttt{ass:source-independence} is preserved.  It also preserves Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy}: if \(rY\) were almost surely constant for \(r\ne0\), then \(Y=r^{-1}(rY)\) would be almost surely constant.  It preserves Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nongaussianity} for the same reason: if \(rY\) were Gaussian, then \(Y=r^{-1}(rY)\) would be Gaussian.  If centering or Assumption \texttt{ass:source-second-moment} is imposed on the subfamily under consideration, it too is preserved, since
\[
 \mathbb E[rY]=r\mathbb E[Y],
 \qquad
 \mathbb E[(rY)^2]=r^2\mathbb E[Y^2].
 \tag{5}
\]

The endogenous vector solving (1) satisfies the transformed equations sample by sample.  Indeed, using the equations for \(X_2\) and \(X_1\), respectively,
\[
 \alpha X_2+\eta_1
 =b^{-1}(X_2-\varepsilon_2)=X_1,
 \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \gamma L+\beta X_1+\eta_2
 =-ca^{-1}L+a^{-1}(X_1-\varepsilon_1)=X_2.
 \tag{7}
\]
Also \(L=\eta_L\) and \(X_3=\delta L+\eta_3\).  Thus (6)--(7) are precisely the \(H_\star\) equations and the two observed vectors agree almost surely.

The transformation stays in the exact-support class.  All four coefficients in (3) are nonzero by (2), and
\[
 1-\alpha\beta
 =1-\frac1{ab}
 =\frac{ab-1}{ab}\ne0.
 \tag{8}
\]
For completeness, regime solvability does not conceal a stability condition.  Because \(S\subseteq\{X_1,X_2,X_3\}\) and the only directed cycle is the \(X_1,X_2\) two-cycle, direct expansion of the relevant principal structural matrix gives
\[
 \det Q^{G_\star}_{V\setminus S,V\setminus S}
 =\begin{cases}
 1-ab,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}=\varnothing,\\
 1,&S\cap\{X_1,X_2\}\ne\varnothing,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{9}
\]
and the analogous determinant for \(H_\star\) is obtained by replacing \(ab\) by \(\alpha\beta\).  Equations (2), (8), and (9) verify Assumption \texttt{ass:regime-solvability} for every observed intervention target.

Conversely, let an arbitrary \(H_\star\) mechanism have nonzero coefficients \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\) and \(1-\alpha\beta\ne0\).  Set
\[
 a=\beta^{-1},\qquad b=\alpha^{-1},\qquad
 c=-\gamma\beta^{-1},\qquad d=\delta,
 \tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \varepsilon_L=\eta_L,\qquad
 \varepsilon_1=-\beta^{-1}\eta_2,\qquad
 \varepsilon_2=-\alpha^{-1}\eta_1,\qquad
 \varepsilon_3=\eta_3.
 \tag{11}
\]
The quantities in (10) are nonzero and
\[
 1-ab=1-\frac1{\alpha\beta}
 =\frac{\alpha\beta-1}{\alpha\beta}\ne0.
 \tag{12}
\]
The preservation argument following (4) applies to (11), and substitution shows that (10)--(11) invert (3)--(4).  We have therefore constructed a bijection of the entire admissible observational parameter spaces, not merely of generic subsets or their closures.  Equations (6)--(7) show equality of the coupled observed solutions.  Definitions \texttt{def:response-kernel-tuple} and \texttt{def:graph-law-set} now yield
\[
 \mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(G_\star)
 =\mathcal P_{\{\varnothing\}}(H_\star).
 \tag{13}
\]

We next record the finite-moment covariance calculation.  Assumption \texttt{ass:perfect-intervention} says that \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=z)\) replaces only the equation for \(X_1\).  For (1), the unaffected equations give
\[
 X_2=bz+\varepsilon_2,\qquad
 X_3=d\varepsilon_L+\varepsilon_3.
 \tag{14}
\]
The first variable in (14) is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\varepsilon_2)\), and the second is measurable with respect to \(\sigma(\varepsilon_L,\varepsilon_3)\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:source-independence} therefore makes \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) independent, without any moment condition.  If Assumption \texttt{ass:source-second-moment} is imposed for this covariance clause, bilinearity of covariance and independence give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{G_\star}(X_2,X_3)
 =d\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_L)
  +\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_2,\varepsilon_3)=0.
 \tag{15}
\]

For an arbitrary \(H_\star\) mechanism, surgical intervention gives
\[
 X_2=\gamma\eta_L+\beta z+\eta_2,\qquad
 X_3=\delta\eta_L+\eta_3.
 \tag{16}
\]
When the sources in (16) have finite second moments, source independence gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}_{H_\star}(X_2,X_3)
 &=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)
   +\gamma\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_L,\eta_3)
   +\delta\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_L)
   +\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_2,\eta_3)\\
 &=\gamma\delta\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{17}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy} and square integrability give \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_L)>0\), so (17) is nonzero.  For the paired mechanism (3)--(4), \(\gamma=-c/a\), \(\delta=d\), and \(\eta_L=\varepsilon_L\).  By the definition of \(\sigma_L^2\), equation (17) becomes
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}_{H_\star}(X_2,X_3)
 =-\frac ca d\sigma_L^2\ne0.
 \tag{18}
\]

It remains to prove separation of the full model sets when their general source laws need not possess moments.  Take the legal coefficients
\[
 a=\frac12,\qquad b=\frac13,\qquad c=d=1,
 \tag{19}
\]
and let the four \(G_\star\) sources be mutually independent symmetric random signs.  Each source is centered, bounded, nonconstant, non-Gaussian, and has finite second moment.  Equations (9) and (19) show that this mechanism is solvable in every regime.  Let \(\mathbf K^G\) denote its joint response-kernel tuple.  At \(z=0\), (14) shows that the \(X_2\) and \(X_3\) coordinates of its singleton-intervention kernel are square integrable and have covariance zero.

Suppose for contradiction that \(\mathbf K^G\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)\).  By Definition \texttt{def:graph-law-set}, one \(H_\star\) mechanism with one common source tuple must then reproduce every component of \(\mathbf K^G\).  In particular, its kernel at \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=0)\) has the same joint law.  Hence each variable on the right side of (16), with \(z=0\), is square integrable.  Apply Lemma \texttt{lem:square-integrable-independent-summands} first to the independent summands \(\delta\eta_L\) and \(\eta_3\), and then to the independent summands \(\gamma\eta_L\) and \(\eta_2\).  It follows that
\[
 \mathbb E[\eta_L^2]<\infty,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\eta_2^2]<\infty,\qquad
 \mathbb E[\eta_3^2]<\infty,
 \tag{20}
\]
where division by \(\gamma^2\) or \(\delta^2\) is valid because Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-support} gives \(\gamma\delta\ne0\).  Thus the covariance calculation (17) is licensed even though no moment condition was imposed on the ambient population class.  Assumption \texttt{ass:source-nondegeneracy} makes the resulting variance strictly positive, so (17) gives a nonzero covariance, contradicting equality with the covariance-zero \(G_\star\) kernel.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbf K^G\notin\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star),
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(G_\star)\ne
 \mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(H_\star)
 \quad\text{whenever }\{X_1\}\in\mathcal I.
 \tag{21}
\]

The causal objects in (13) and (21) are sets of population perfect-intervention response kernels, not observational regressions.  No treatment-overlap or positivity condition is needed because intervention values are externally fixed.  All matrices are finite dimensional, every inversion was justified by (2), (8), (9), or (12), and no boundary or limiting argument is used.
body.justification: A uniform all-parameter witness proves that the interventional quotient is strictly finer than the observational quotient without relying on genericity.
body.gap: The zero-allowed version of this witness is false at zero pivots; the claim here is restricted to the newly specified exact nonzero support and re-proves the full parameter-space bijection directly.
body.consumer: The witness tells perturbation planners when one observed-node intervention resolves a feedback reversal and latent-parent ambiguity that no observational sample can resolve.
